extracted.intended_audience: federal employees, agency EEO officials, attorneys/representatives, and individuals involved in EEOC mixed-case appeals, appeals to the Commission, or filing civil actions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory procedures and substantive requirements in 29 C.F.R. part 1614 governing mixed-case processing, petitions from MSPB decisions, appeals to the EEOC, Special Panel procedures, time limits for civil actions, and remedies and enforcement for discrimination findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of right to contact EEO counselor
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall promptly notify the individual in writing of the right to contact an EEO counselor within 45 days of receipt of this notice and to file an EEO complaint, subject to § 1614.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the person filed his or her appeal with MSPB shall be deemed to be the date of initial contact with the counselor. If MSPB dismisses a timely appeal for jurisdictional reasons, the agency shall reissue a notice under § 1614.108(f) giving the individual the right to elect between a hearing before an administrative judge and an immediate final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of mixed case complaints per §1614.107
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may dismiss a mixed case complaint for the reasons contained in, and under the conditions prescribed in, § 1614.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dismissal is based on prior election of MSPB procedures, follow the specific procedures in §1614.303 and notify complainant of right to petition EEOC to review MSPB final decision on discrimination issues; dismissal of mixed case complaints is not appealable to the Commission except where §1614.107(a)(4) was applied to a non-mixed case matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency handling when MSPB jurisdiction questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the agency or MSPB administrative judge questions MSPB's jurisdiction over an appeal on the same matter, the agency shall hold the mixed case complaint in abeyance until MSPB rules on jurisdiction, notify the complainant, and instruct him or her to bring the allegation to MSPB; processing time limits are tolled during abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency decision to hold the complaint in abeyance is not appealable to EEOC. If MSPB finds jurisdiction, agency dismisses pursuant to §1614.107(a)(4) and advises of right to petition EEOC; if MSPB finds no jurisdiction, agency recommences processing as a non-mixed case EEO complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency notice when accepting mixed case complaint (rights/advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: When agency accepts a mixed case complaint it shall advise the complainant that: (i) if a final decision is not issued within 120 days of filing the complainant may appeal to MSPB or file a civil action (but not both); and (ii) if dissatisfied with agency final decision the complainant may appeal to MSPB (not EEOC) within 30 days of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon completion of investigation, the notice in accordance with §1614.108(f) will advise complainant that a final decision will be issued within 45 days without a hearing. At time of final decision agency shall advise right to appeal to MSPB within 30 days and right to file civil action as provided in §1614.310(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to EEOC from MSPB decisions — who may file
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who have received a final decision from the MSPB on a mixed case appeal or on the appeal of a final decision on a mixed case complaint under 5 CFR part 1201, subpart E and 5 U.S.C. 7702 may petition EEOC to consider that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EEOC will not accept appeals from MSPB dismissals without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of filing petitions from MSPB decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing shall be made by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Office of Federal Operations, Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, P.O. Box 77960, Washington, DC 20013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict certified mail filing requirement for petitions for review of MSPB decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file petition to Commission from MSPB decision
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must be filed with the Commission either within 30 days of receipt of the final decision of the MSPB or within 30 days of when the decision of a MSPB field office becomes final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty-day filing deadline; timely service requirements apply (see §1614.303(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition for review must be served upon all individuals and parties on the MSPB's service list by certified mail on or before the filing with the Commission, and the Clerk of the Board, MSPB, 1615 M Street, NW., Washington, DC 20419, and the petitioner must certify as to the date and method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must certify date and method of service; service must be by certified mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for petitions (§1614.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must be written or typed, may use any format including a simple letter; petitioners are encouraged to use EEOC Form 573. Petitions must contain name/address of petitioner and representative, a statement of reasons why MSPB decision is incorrect (only with regard to discrimination issues), a copy of the MSPB decision, and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of reasons is limited to discrimination issues based on protected categories listed in the regulation (race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, pregnancy/related conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission consideration procedures for MSPB petitions (§1614.305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a petition is filed, the Commission will examine it and determine whether the Commission will consider the decision of the MSPB; an agency may oppose within 15 days of receipt by Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission determines within 30 days whether to consider. If it decides to consider, within 60 days it will review the MSPB record (supplemented if necessary) and either concur or issue a decision that differs if MSPB's decision is incorrect as a matter of law or unsupported by the record. Commission may refer case back to MSPB for additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to Special Panel when MSPB reaffirms (§1614.306)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the MSPB reaffirms its decision under 5 CFR 1201.162(a)(2) with or without modification, the matter shall be immediately certified to the Special Panel established pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 7702(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon certification the Board must transmit the administrative record including factual record and transcripts, the decisions by Board and Commission, and transcripts of oral arguments or legal briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Special Panel (§1614.307)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Panel is composed of: (1) a Chairman appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent (6-year term); (2) one member of the MSPB designated by the Chairman of the Board each time a panel is convened; and (3) one member of the EEOC designated by the Chairman of the Commission each time a panel is convened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designations must be made within five days of certification and letters of designation served on the Chairman of Special Panel and the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Panel time limit and expedited procedures (§1614.308)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Special Panel shall issue a decision within 45 days of the matter being certified to it. The Chairman may suspend rules in this subpart to expedite a decision, except where a rule is required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short statutory timelines govern Panel proceedings; procedural flexibility allowed for good cause or expedition; administrative assistance provided by MSPB and EEOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and service requirements before Special Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall file the original and six copies of all submissions with the Clerk, MSPB; one copy served on other parties; certificate of service must accompany submissions; service may be by mail or personal delivery during normal business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to short time limits, parties must file by overnight delivery if filing by mail. Date of filing determined by overnight mailing order date; personal delivery filing date is date received by Clerk, MSPB. Briefs for the Special Panel must be filed within 15 days of Board's certification order; responsive pleadings ordinarily not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument and post-argument submissions before Special Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to oral argument if desired and must indicate request at time of filing brief or within 15 days of certification order; Chairman determines time/place and time to be allowed; no post-argument submissions except by order of Chairman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short timelines mean responsive filings and post-argument submissions are generally restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Panel record maintenance and administrative costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall maintain the official record and transmit two copies of each submission to each Special Panel member; MSPB and EEOC shall provide reasonable administrative resources; Board and EEOC responsible for administrative costs and, to extent practicable, shall equally divide costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chairman of the Special Panel resolves cost allocation disputes between Board and EEOC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of Special Panel decision (§1614.309)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board shall, upon receipt of the decision of the Special Panel, order the agency concerned to take any action appropriate to carry out the decision of the Panel; the Board's regulations regarding enforcement of a final order shall apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 5 CFR part 1201, subpart E for enforcement regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time triggers and conditions for filing civil actions (§1614.310)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual authorized by 5 U.S.C. 7702 to file a civil action may do so under multiple time triggers: (a) within 30 days of receipt of a final agency decision unless appeal filed with MSPB; (b) within 30 days of receipt of notice of MSPB final decision if individual does not file EEOC petition; (c)-(f) within 30 days of various Commission/MSPB/Special Panel notices as specified; (g)-(i) after 120/180 days or 180 days from filing petition under certain no-decision circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated triggers must be followed precisely; different triggers apply depending on whether appeals/petitions or agency/MSPB/EEOC actions have occurred; see the multiple subparagraphs for exact circumstances and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal to the Commission (§1614.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant may appeal an agency's final action or dismissal of a complaint. An agency may appeal as provided in §1614.110(a). Class agents, class members, or agencies may appeal decisions relating to class complaints as specified; grievants may appeal certain negotiated grievance outcomes when an issue of employment discrimination was raised, subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal rights vary by status (complainant, agency, class agent, class member, grievant) and by procedural posture; some matters remain non-appealable under this part if pending in other processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for appeals to the Commission (§1614.402)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals described in §1614.401(a) and (c) must be filed within 30 days of receipt of the dismissal, final action or decision. Appeals described in §1614.401(b) must be filed within 40 days of receipt of the hearing file and decision. Other specific timelines for appeals are provided, and when represented by counsel the time is calculated from the attorney's receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation of the appeal period differs if the appellant is represented; specific exceptions exist (e.g., appeals following notices of noncompliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to file an appeal to the Commission (§1614.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must file an appeal with the Director, Office of Federal Operations, EEOC, at the specified P.O. Box, or electronically/by personal delivery/facsimile; should use EEOC Form 573 and indicate what is being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant must furnish copy to opposing party at same time and certify date/method of service. Untimely appeals are dismissed. Statements/briefs deadlines: complainant's within 30 days of filing notice; agency's within 20 days. OFO will accept facsimile statements/briefs if no more than 10 pages. Agency must submit complaint file within 30 days. Parties are required/encouraged to submit digital formats acceptable to Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellate procedure and supplementation of record (§1614.404)
rubrics_metrics.description: OFO will review the complaint file and written statements/briefs; the Commission may supplement the record by letters/memoranda, investigation, remand, or other procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party fails without good cause to comply or respond fully/timely, OFO may draw adverse inferences, consider matters established for opposing party, issue decisions (fully or partially) in favor of opposing party, or take other appropriate actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and content of Commission decisions on appeals (§1614.405)
rubrics_metrics.description: OFO shall issue a written decision setting forth its reasons. Decisions shall be based on the preponderance of the evidence; de novo review applies to agency final actions except factual findings by an administrative judge under §1614.109(i) are reviewed under substantial evidence standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finding discrimination, include appropriate remedies and indicate entitlement to interest, attorney's fees or costs. Decisions must state date of issuance, inform complainant of civil action rights, and be transmitted to complainant and agency via Portal or first class mail depending on consent. Decisions on class complaint appeals issued within 90 days. Reconsideration may be requested within 30 days on narrow grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and timing for Commission reconsideration (§1614.405(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request reconsideration within 30 days of receipt of a Commission decision; Commission may grant if party demonstrates a clearly erroneous interpretation of material fact or law, or that decision will have substantial impact on agency policies/practices/operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration is discretionary and limited to the stated grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute-specific time limits for civil actions (§1614.407 and §1614.408)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Title VII, ADEA, Rehabilitation Act, GINA, and PWFA, complainants/agents/claimants may file civil actions within 90 days of receipt of agency final action, after 180 days if no final action, within 90 days of Commission final decision, or after 180 days from filing an appeal with Commission if no final decision. For Equal Pay Act, civil action is within two years (three if willful) of alleged violation; back wages limited to two years (three if willful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various withdrawal/recalculation rules apply (e.g., withdrawing appeal to file suit). Filing a complaint or appeal does not toll Equal Pay Act filing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of filing a civil action on Commission processing (§1614.409)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a civil action under §§1614.407 or 1614.408 shall terminate Commission processing of the appeal. A Commission decision on an appeal issued after a complainant files suit in district court will not be enforceable by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If private suit is filed subsequent to filing an appeal and prior to a final Commission decision, complainant should notify the Commission in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of full relief when discrimination found (§1614.501(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency or the Commission finds discrimination in an individual case, the agency shall provide full relief which shall include in appropriate circumstances: (1) notification to employees in affected facility of right to be free from unlawful discrimination and assurance nonrecurrence; (2) commitment to corrective/curative/preventive action; (3) unconditional offer of placement to each identified victim of discrimination in the position they would have occupied or substantially equivalent position; (4) payment on a make-whole basis for any loss of earnings; and (5) commitment to cease the specific unlawful employment practice found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief elements are illustrative and agencies must provide full relief 'in appropriate circumstances'—implementation details follow in subsequent paragraphs for applicants and employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for applicants (§1614.501(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When agency finds an applicant was discriminated against, the agency shall offer the applicant the position they would have occupied absent discrimination or a substantially equivalent position unless clear and convincing evidence shows the applicant would not have been selected even absent discrimination. Offer must be in writing; individual has 15 days to accept or decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, appointment retroactive to date applicant would have been hired; back pay computed per 5 CFR 550.805; if declined, agency shall award back pay from would-have-been appointment date until offer decline, subject to limitations. Back pay for applicants under Title VII or Rehab Act may not extend earlier than two years prior to complaint filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for employees (§1614.501(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When agency finds an employee discriminated against, relief shall include but not be limited to: nondiscriminatory placement with back pay (unless clear/convincing evidence shows action would have been taken anyway), cancellation of unwarranted personnel action and restoration, expunction of adverse materials, and full opportunity to participate in denied employee benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back pay computed per 5 CFR 550.805; back pay liability under Title VII or Rehabilitation Act limited to two years prior to complaint filing. Even if action would have been taken absent discrimination, agency shall eliminate discriminatory practice and ensure nonrecurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's mitigation burden (§1614.501(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency has the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the complainant has failed to mitigate his or her damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must demonstrate failure to mitigate; burden is preponderance of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards of attorney's fees and costs (§1614.501(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions apply to Title VII and Rehabilitation Act: agency, administrative judge, or Commission may award reasonable attorney's fees (including expert witness fees) and other costs incurred in processing the complaint. A finding of discrimination raises a presumption of entitlement; any award shall be paid by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees allowable only for services of members of the Bar and supervised law clerks/paralegals/law students; not allowable for services of Federal Government employees. Fees generally payable for services after filing written complaint provided reasonable notice of representation given, with limited exceptions for pre-complaint work under certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and review of attorney's fees and costs (§1614.501(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When entitlement to fees/costs determined, attorney submits verified statement and affidavit itemizing charges within 30 days; agency may respond within 30 days. The agency or administrative judge shall decide amount within 60 days, include notice of appeal rights, and specify reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount calculated using hours reasonably expended × reasonable hourly rate (strong presumption). In limited circumstances amount may be adjusted for degree of success, quality of representation, and long agency delay. Costs awarded limited to those authorized by 28 U.S.C. 1920; witness fees per 28 U.S.C. 1821 with exception for Federal employee on duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with final Commission decisions (§1614.502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relief ordered in a final Commission decision is mandatory and binding on the agency except as provided. Failure to implement ordered relief shall be subject to judicial enforcement as specified in §1614.503(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency requests reconsideration and case involves continuing removal/separation/suspension beyond request date and decision orders retroactive restoration, agency shall comply to extent of temporary/conditional restoration pending reconsideration. Service under temporary/conditional restoration is credited toward probation/trial period and related service requirements if Commission upholds decision.
